messages:
Maria: Heads-up: I noticed a bunch of 401 spikes tied to ephemeral SA keys last night. Looks like leases weren't being renewed in edge regions.
Jon: ugh. Any pattern on which customers/regions?
Maria: mostly eu-west-1 + a few p99 latencies hitting our token service around 02:00 UTC.
Ash: Was the renewal cron failing or the heartbeat from the key proxy?
Maria: proxy heartbeats stopped for ~6m then resumed, but the console showed "active" for the keys which confused users.
Sam: That sounds like visibility mismatch — lease expired but console cache still flagged it active. Could be our cache TTL vs token server TTL.
Jon: Can we add a lease-heartbeat metric to the key service and a small panel in Console? Even a status column "last heartbeat" would help support.
Ash: Agreed. Suggest metrics: last_heartbeat_unix, lease_expires_unix, proxy_seen_timestamp. Then a simple alert if last_heartbeat < now - 60s for production proxies.
Maria: +1. Also users saw a generic 401 message. We should map 401 -> "lease expired" when applicable so Console can show actionable text rather than generic auth failure.
Sam: For UX, show red dot next to key with hover: "Last heartbeat 6m ago — lease may have expired. Click to renew." Add a one-click renew in the key row that triggers ephemeral reissue.
Jon: One-click renew is nice but need CSRF/consent check for org-level keys. Could gate behind a small modal with audit log link.
Ash: Implementation notes: token-service already emits heartbeat events via Kafka topic key-heartbeats. We can pipe to observability and also have the Console read a compact KV in redis for last_seen to keep UI latency low.
Maria: Perf question: do we risk extra load if Console pings redis for every page view? Maybe cache in frontend for 30s.
Sam: Yep, 30s cache + websocket for key row updates when renew happens. That avoids heavy polling.
Jon: For routing policies: when a proxy misses heartbeat, should we route to fallback pool or return explicit 401? Current behavior is silent failover which caused misleading console state.
Ash: I'd prefer explicit failure for expirations. Silent failover is fine for transient infra issues, but lease expiry means the credential is invalid and should be surfaced.
Maria: OK: policy proposal: if last_heartbeat > ttl => return 401 (auth error) and emit event auth.expired with reason=heartbeat. If last_heartbeat missing but proxy reachable => fallback route with warning.
Sam: Sounds good. We should also add telemetry tag "lease_renew_flow": manual|auto|expired so we can run a quick query on how often renewals are manual.
Jon: Could we add a tiny canary rollout for the UI change? Maybe 10% of orgs see the new "last heartbeat" column first.
Maria: Yes. We'll ship backend events first (heartbeat metric + auth.expired event) then UI canary for 10%.
Ash: Dev plan: 1) stream last_heartbeat into observability + produce auth.expired event. 2) add redis last_seen compact KV and API endpoint /v1/keys/:id/last_seen. 3) Console: new column + hover + one-click renew modal. 4) Telemetry tags.
Sam: I'll mock the UX in Sketch and drop screenshots here.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started for branch feature/key-heartbeat-metrics (build 2174). :rocket:
Maria: Thanks. Can someone own the RFC for audit implications? One-click renew should create an audit entry and require a scope check.
Jon: I'll own the RFC and ensure we don't bypass org consent.
Ash: I'll take the backend pieces. Sam — Console owner?
Sam: Yep I'll take the UI + telemetry wiring.
Maria: sweet. Timeline? Can we aim for backend metrics + event in 2 sprints, UI canary end of sprint 3?
Jon: sounds reasonable.
Maria: OK closing this thread — please add tasks to the eng-platform board and tag with #auth-lease.
Sam: will do :+1:
